Title: Phishing Email Attacks
Text: Phishing emails trick people into revealing passwords, bank details, and private information. Attackers imitate trusted companies and create urgent messages with malicious links. Users should inspect sender addresses, avoid unexpected attachments, and report suspicious email to the security team.

Title: Malware and Antivirus Protection
Text: Malware is harmful software that can steal data, damage files, or monitor a computer. Viruses, worms, spyware, and trojans are common malware types. Updated antivirus tools, safe downloads, software patches, and regular scans help protect devices from infection.

Title: Ransomware Incident Response
Text: Ransomware encrypts files and demands payment to restore access. Organizations should maintain offline backups, patch vulnerable systems, restrict administrator privileges, and train employees to recognize suspicious attachments. During an incident, isolate affected machines and follow a documented recovery plan.

Title: Network Firewalls and Intrusion Detection
Text: A network firewall filters incoming and outgoing traffic according to security rules. Intrusion detection systems monitor network activity for unusual patterns and possible attacks. Combining firewall policies, network segmentation, logging, and regular rule reviews improves network protection.

Title: Encryption and Data Privacy
Text: Encryption converts readable information into coded data that can only be recovered with the appropriate key. Strong encryption protects files, messages, and data moving across networks. Privacy programs should also limit data collection, control access, and securely delete information that is no longer needed.

Title: Password Managers and Strong Authentication
Text: Strong passwords should be long, unique, and difficult to guess. A password manager stores credentials securely and helps people avoid reusing passwords. Multi-factor authentication adds another verification step, reducing the risk that a stolen password will allow account access.

Title: Cloud Security and Access Control
Text: Cloud security requires careful identity management, access control, encryption, and continuous monitoring. Teams should grant users only the permissions needed for their roles. Secure configuration, audit logs, backup policies, and timely updates reduce the chance of cloud data exposure.

Title: Public Wi-Fi and Safe Browsing
Text: Public Wi-Fi may expose users to fake hotspots and traffic interception. People should verify network names, use secure HTTPS websites, avoid sensitive transactions on untrusted networks, and keep device software updated. A trusted virtual private network can add protection when using public connections.

Title: Data Breaches and Security Awareness
Text: A data breach occurs when unauthorized people access confidential information. Weak passwords, misconfigured systems, phishing, and unpatched software can contribute to breaches. Security awareness training, access reviews, incident reporting, and a tested response plan help reduce impact.

Title: Multi-Factor Authentication for Online Accounts
Text: Multi-factor authentication verifies identity using two or more different factors, such as a password and a one-time code or security key. It provides stronger account protection than a password alone. Organizations should enable it for email, administrator accounts, remote access, and important online services.
